Dear [Mrs Drew](/person/443),
I was out all yesterday and could not answer your kind letter, nor thank you for the excellent paper, which I have ventured to take to [Mrs Sumner](/person/1381), who is really the parent of the [Mother’s Union](/organisation/31). I could not use it for the [Monthly Packet](/periodical/52) as I am obliged scrupulously to keep that for young girls’ reading; but there is a yet undeveloped notion of starting some kind of paper, leaflet or the like for the Mothers and if this were done, I hope we might have the use of your admirable paper.

Mrs Sumner has brought into the Mother’s Union most of the tradesmen’s wives of all degrees, and this seem to be very helpful
Yours very truly

C M Yonge


[^1]: The letter must postdate Mary Drew\'s marriage on 25 December 1885, and predate the letter to her of 1 February 1888 which refers to the forthcoming publication of the [Mothers\' Union Journal](/periodical/93).
